subject: Fed hikes to 4%, and Canada now trails by 1.6 points
bodyMarkdown:
The U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates on Wednesday for the first time since 2023, and the Bank of Canada does not speak again until October 28. The space between those two facts is where your mortgage renewal and your U.S. dollar purchases now live.

## What the Fed actually did

CNBC reported Wednesday that the Federal Open Market Committee lifted its target range a quarter point, to 3.75% to 4%, on a 12 to 0 vote. It is the first increase since July 2023. The Fed's implementation note set the rate paid on reserve balances at 3.90%, effective today. Seeking Alpha's account of the press conference has Chair Kevin Warsh saying inflation is "too high" and "has been for too long," and, asked about the path from here, that he is "not in the forward guidance business." The **dot plot**, the anonymous grid where each official marks where they think rates belong, showed 16 of 18 participants expecting another increase before the end of the year. Warsh still declines to submit a dot of his own. Reuters reported that a December move is now fully priced in.

## The loonie took it on the chin

Reuters reported Wednesday that the Canadian dollar fell about 0.5% to 1.3990 per U.S. dollar, or 71.48 U.S. cents, touching its weakest level since August 7, while the U.S. dollar hit a seven-week high against its major peers. None of that is mysterious. The Fed's new midpoint is 3.875% and the Bank of Canada has sat at 2.25% since it cut in October 2025, so the gap is now roughly 1.6 percentage points, and money goes where it is paid more. CNBC reported the 10-year Treasury yield back above 5% and the two-year up more than seven basis points to 4.738%. A cheaper loonie raises the price of everything Canada buys abroad, and Canada buys a lot of what it eats and almost everything it drives.

## What the Bank of Canada is weighing

The Bank of Canada also published its summary of deliberations on Wednesday, covering the September 2 decision to hold at 2.25% for a seventh straight meeting. BNN Bloomberg reported that Governing Council spent much of that discussion on the reignited tariff fight with the United States and what it could do to business and consumer confidence, with the economy entering this round in decent shape, housing picking back up and the private sector still adding jobs. Statistics Canada reported on September 14 that inflation held at 3.0% in August, with gasoline up 22.8% from a year earlier and rent up 2.8%. Strip out gasoline and the number is 2.4%. RBC Economics does not expect a Canadian hike before 2027. I think that call is right, and I also think it leaves Canada exposed.

## The takeaway

Watch the five-year Government of Canada bond yield, lately around 3.6% and close to a 52-week high, because that is what sets fixed mortgage rates, and Canadian Mortgage Trends reported this month that lenders have already been raising them. If you renew in the next six months, lock a rate hold now instead of waiting on October 28, which is unlikely to rescue you. If you are buying U.S. dollars for a trip or for tuition, 71 cents is a worse starting point than August was. And if the Fed goes again in December while Ottawa holds, the gap widens and Canada ends up importing American inflation through the exchange rate, whether the Bank of Canada likes it or not.
